text:
Kai Wu: Heads up — I'm proposing a change to the gateway's region arbitration logic. Short version: 1) honor x-region-prefer header if tenant-level policy allows 2) else prefer client's geographic region 3) else use lowest-latency eligible region measured by probes 4) finally fallback to tenant-configured backup region. Need feedback on header precedence and what to show in Console rollout UI :thinking:

Anya Patel: Why is header above client geo? curious about hijack risk if header set by proxies

Kai Wu: Good point. The idea: header only supersedes geo when it's signed by tenant (we add signature/kms). Unsigned headers should be treated as hint. So precedence: signed header > tenant preference > client-geo > latency > backup.

Maria Gomez: Can we avoid signed-headers complexity for now? Maybe a tenant opt-in toggle in Console that says "honor client-signed region headers"

Jordan Lee: For telemetry: we need a metric for "region-arbitration-reason" tag per request. Otherwise can't tell how often we pick latency vs geo vs header. Also surface top-3 chosen regions in the route trace.

Kai Wu: Agreed. Proposed telemetry fields: region_chosen, reason_tag (header|tenant|client_geo|latency|backup), probe_latency_ms, probe_variance_ms

sre-bot: Note: adding reason_tag will increase log cardinality. Suggest sampling or aggregation buckets.

Anya Patel: On quotas: if we route to backup region, do we charge quota on original tenant region or the actual execution region? Need policy for billing and per-region capacity accounting.

Kai Wu: Plan: always attribute usage to tenant's billable region (tenant.region_id). But increment a per-region capacity counter for the region that ran the job (for autoscaling/alerts). This decouples billing and capacity.

Maria Gomez: UX: in Console rollout flow, we should show a "Regional arbitration policy" preview with examples: where header present signed=true, header present unsigned, client in EU but tenant prefers US, high-latency probe causing failover. Small simulated list would help SREs approve.

Jordan Lee: +1 for simulations. Also add historical ejection chart: count of requests ejected by latency per region per day.

Kai Wu: Here's a rough route config I sketched:

```yaml
route:
  match: path_prefix: /v1/generate
  region_policy:
    honor_signed_header: true
    header_name: X-Region-Prefer
    precedence: [signed_header, tenant_pref, client_geo, latency_probe, tenant_backup]
    latency_slo_ms: 120
    latency_probe_weight: 0.7
``` 

Anya Patel: LGTM. One more: how do we handle agent SDKs that set header to "local"? Should map "local" -> client_geo

Kai Wu: Yes map alias values. We'll document common aliases in SDKs.

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled for 2061243000 to eng-platform canary cluster for 3h :rocket:

Maria Gomez: Quick ops question — if tenant_backup is used, do we enforce tenant's data residency constraints? Probably yes, can't run in a region with conflicting residency rules.

Kai Wu: Correct — residency constraints are hard guardrails. region_policy only considers eligible_regions after residency filters.

Jordan Lee: Action items: (1) Add reason_tag in telemetry + sampling plan (2) Console: simulation UI mock (3) Quotas: billing attribution doc (4) Residency filter enforcement tests. I'll open follow-up tasks.

Kai Wu: Thanks. If no objections I'll start a PR for config + telemetry tomorrow. :thumbsup:
